item.text: I found the main split: MongoDB and Redis already treat `[]` as “all fields” in their helper, while Postgres aggregates over the requested field list and returns `null` for an empty list. The public `getObject` and `getObjects` methods also currently ignore a `fields` argument. I’m checking the callback adapter and existing missing-key tests before finalizing the diagnosis.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc "sed -n '1,200p' src/promisify.js && git status --short && nl -ba src/database/postgres/hash.js | sed -n '70,195p'"

/bin/bash -lc "cat > .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'
Fault localization complete. No project source or tests changed.

Likely files: src/database/mongo/hash.js, src/database/redis/hash.js, src/database/postgres/hash.js. All getObject/getObjects signatures omit fields. Mongo/Redis getObjectsFields already treat [] as full object and preserve input order, but selected-field paths return an object of null fields for missing keys. Postgres getObjectFields/getObjectsFields use jsonb_object_agg over UNNEST(fields), so [] produces null instead of full data; omitted fields can also fail because fields is passed as a query parameter or iterated. Existing Postgres getObject/getObjects query full data directly and preserve order via WITH ORDINALITY.

Fix behavior to cover: optional fields argument and callback compatibility, full object for [] or omitted fields through all four methods, selected fields only with null for absent field names, null/falsy missing-key result for public getObject/getObjects, input order and duplicates, all three backends. Existing tests in test/database/hash.js cover selected helper fields and missing fields but not [] or selected public methods. Full integration tests were not run because the suite requires database configuration and live backend services.
EOF"

item.text:
The fault is in the three backend hash implementations: [MongoDB](/app/src/database/mongo/hash.js:64), [Redis](/app/src/database/redis/hash.js:64), and [Postgres](/app/src/database/postgres/hash.js:73). Their `getObject` and `getObjects` methods do not accept or forward `fields`. Postgres also turns an empty field list into `null` in its field helpers; MongoDB and Redis already treat `[]` as a full-object request.

A fix should cover omitted and empty `fields`, selected fields with `null` for absent names, missing keys, and input order across all three backends. There is one compatibility detail: existing helper tests expect an object of null fields for a missing key when specific fields are requested, while the requested public `getObject` and `getObjects` behavior is falsy.

I recorded the findings in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). I did not edit project source or tests because this run’s instructions restrict it to fault localization. Integration tests were not run.
